subject: MerchantHQ - urgent: 5xx/429 burst during peak queries (GPU pressure)
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@merchanthq.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@merchanthq.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:12:34 -0800
Subject: Spike of 5xx / 429 across production during 08:00-08:10 PST

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sudden spike of 500/502/429 responses from your inference endpoints from ~08:00 to 08:10 PST this morning. It affected our checkout feature (high QPS) and caused ~12 minutes of elevated timeouts for users. We attached a screenshot and p99 export; traces are in the zip.

What we observed:
- Rapid increase in retries from our side as clients retried, which made the spike worse.
- Error body shows: "backend: instance overloaded / timeout" and intermittent 429s.
- We saw requests routed to "rdw-dedicated-pool-11" and a few fallbacks.

This is high severity for us — can you confirm root cause and a mitigation timeline? We are ready to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alice Jenkins
Head of Platform Ops, MerchantHQ
Attachments: screenshot-500.png (png), p99-latency.csv (csv), debug-traces.zip (zip)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice.jenkins@merchanthq.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:22:10 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx / 429 across production during 08:00-08:10 PST

Folks — escalating. MerchantHQ reports a short, severe burst of 5xx/429 on a Dedicated pool during their morning peak. Attachments from their team show retry amplification and p99 jumps.

Immediate asks:
1) Jonas / infra: please confirm whether the Dedicated GPU pool for MerchantHQ experienced node preemption/eviction or autoscaler lag.
2) Vivek / runtime: check if prefix caching or KV cache evictions correlate with the spike. Any recent kernel selection changes rolled to this pool?
3) Marissa: please coordinate comms with Alice; confirm whether they want credits or configuration changes while we investigate.

I'll open a PagerDuty incident and join the call in 10.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice.jenkins@merchanthq.com
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 08:35:41 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx / 429 across production during 08:00-08:10 PST

On Tue, Nov 9, 2027 at 08:22 AM Soojin Lee wrote:
> Folks — escalating. MerchantHQ reports a short, severe burst of 5xx/429 on a Dedicated pool during their morning peak.

I pulled infra logs and here's the early summary:
- Around 07:59:30 UTC we saw a rapid queuing increase on pool rdw-dedicated-pool-11. The autoscaler started scale-up but one GPU instance failed health checks and was removed. That removal reduced total capacity for ~55s while replacement spun up.
- During the replacement window we hit transient OOM/accept errors in the runtime which surfaced as 5xx. Simultaneous client retries pushed queue depth beyond safe thresholds, creating 429 responses.
- No config rollouts were targeted to MerchantHQ earlier today.

Immediate mitigations we executed (08:30):
- Temporarily increased max burst capacity for rdw-dedicated-pool-11 by +2 instances (manual override).
- Enabled a faster fallback policy to a lower-cost quantized variant for long-running calls (graceful degrade).
- Applied a short-term queue-backpressure throttle at the front door to reduce retry amplification.

Next steps:
A) Post-mortem runbook to capture exact health-check failure root cause.
B) Look into autoscaler tuning: lower scale-up cooldown, faster warm pool for this account.
C) Propose a per-customer soft QPS cap option to avoid noisy-neighbor retries.

I'll join the live call and share logs.

- Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Infrastructure

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@merchanthq.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:02:17 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx / 429 across production during 08:00-08:10 PST

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the quick signal and artifacts. We pushed a temporary routing change at 08:28 to divert a portion of traffic to a warmed quantized variant; error rates dropped immediately. We're continuing to monitor and will share a short exec note by EOD with root-cause and options (credits, config).

Quick question: do you want a formal SLA exception / credit for the 12-minute impact window? I can draft the comms but want to confirm preferred language.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with more details.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Success, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 14:23:02 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike of 5xx / 429 across production during 08:00-08:10 PST

Summary & next actions for exec note:

Root cause (short): transient capacity loss in rdw-dedicated-pool-11 due to a failed GPU instance during an autoscale-up window. The failure created a ~55s capacity gap; repeated client retries during that gap amplified queues, producing 5xx and 429.

What we did:
- Manual burst override to add two instances and warmed a quantized fallback variant (08:28).
- Short front-door backpressure to reduce retry amplification.
- Post-incident: captured full heap/traces (attached), enabled extended logs for this pool for 30 days, and flagged autoscaler thresholds for tuning.

Permanent mitigations (plan & ETA):
1) Autoscaler tuning (lower cooldown & faster warm pool): rollout in 10 business days after validation in staging.
2) Soft per-account QPS cap configurable via Console (beta): ETA 4 weeks.
3) Health-check resiliency: investigate false-positive health check removal (root cause analysis in 3 business days).

Customer asks: SLA exception and 30-day elevated retention — recommend approval. Also propose we offer MerchantHQ a one-month credit for the incident window and a follow-up operational review.

I'll prepare the EOD exec note and a redacted post-mortem draft.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Runtime & Performance
Attachments: debug-traces.zip, p99-latency.csv
